text: When an order implies a production quota (e.g. "make N items"), add a wait step at the end of the build sized to the real throughput (single inserter ~0.83 items/s caps the machine) so the target count is reached before verification. Consider fast inserters or two input inserters to speed it up.

When powering a build from a distant grid pole, run the power step first (before placing your own poles), or make sure the first new pole is within 7.5 tiles of the grid pole. Wire reach between two poles is the smaller of their two reaches, so a small pole can't reach a medium pole 8+ tiles away. Afterwards, check that the build is on the generator's grid, not on its own unpowered pole network.

When the power source is a distant grid pole, make the power step's first pole a medium pole set within 7.5 tiles of it, and power the build before placing anything else. In the expect checks, ask for a sensible output count and leave a wait step, so a slow line has time to fill the chest before verification.

A power step can leave the new poles on their own dead network, so after it explicitly place a bridging pole within wire reach of both the grid pole and the build's first pole. Check the area's power list: any grid with "generators: none" means the build isn't connected.

Before planning fetches or gathering, check the character's inventory is not nearly full (bulk items like thousands of stone block every pickup) and dump it into chests first using materials already at hand (e.g. take plates from nearby furnace outputs). Before relying on a fuel or resource source, confirm with find that enough of it actually exists and is reachable (e.g. count trees for wood: ~4

For belt or power runs over ~200 tiles, split connect/power into legs of under ~150 tiles via waypoints, and start the power line by placing your own pole next to the target grid's generator (power from=that pole) so the line doesn't latch onto a nearer, different grid. Mining drills have no recipe, so verify them with powered/belt_carries/has_item checks, not "working" with a recipe.

When burner machines are out of fuel and find shows no coal or wood anywhere, don't plan to gather fuel; move some fuel from healthy burners (take coal from their fuel slots) into the dead ones so every site has at least one running. Before any fetch or pickup, make sure the inventory isn't clogged with bulk items, and dump them into chests first.

When the goal is "every site running" and fuel can't be found anywhere, rebalance it at once: take all the fuel out of a few burners at sites with several working ones (keep at least one running per site) and split it so each dead site gets at least one fueled furnace. Don't waste plans gathering wood or coal before checking it exists, and don't bother clearing side problems the count doesn't meas

For belt-routing puzzles where a previous attempt left a tangled partial layout (unpaired undergrounds, unbuilt ghosts), don't patch it: first mine every belt/underground type that is actually on the ground (only types present, or the step fails), then run one route step with all pairs on the clean area. For "get all my scattered sites running", first survey every site with wide area calls and fix all faults in one plan: missing feeders/belt tiles as well as fuel, and a site only counts when all its machines run. When fuel is a fixed pool, spread it evenly across every furnace at once instead of draining whole furnaces, and use explicit counts on refuel/insert, since refuel dumps all the fuel you

When many burner sites must all run and no fuel source exists, do one survey of every site, then a single plan that skims a small equal amount of fuel from every well-stocked burner and tops up every empty or low one. Fixing only the sites reported dead lets the next-lowest site die while you travel.

Don't trust a single power step to link a build to a grid pole more than ~7 tiles away: lay an explicit chain of small poles at most 6 tiles apart from right next to the grid pole into the build, then place the build's own poles. Before submitting, check that every pole in the chain is within wire reach of the next.

When an order says to build machines "off" a belt at a pointed location, put them right beside that belt close to the given point (inserters picking straight off it), not at the belt's far end; verification counts machines near the pointed spot. Never route an output belt so it joins the end of the input belt, or input items will leak into the output chest.

Don't trust a power step to place a pole at the exact target tile; instead explicitly place every build pole yourself, with the first one within 7.5 tiles of a pole you've confirmed (via find) is on the generator grid. Then check that no grid in the area shows "generators: none".

Before powering a build, use find small-electric-pole to locate the grid's existing poles nearest the build, then place your own poles in an explicit chain of hops of 7 tiles or less from one of them, so you don't depend on a power step that may skip poles or leave them on a dead network. Make sure every inserter and machine sits inside some pole's 5x5 supply area.

When an inserter moves items from an existing belt onto a new branch belt, start the new belt one tile beyond the inserter's tile (the inserter's drop tile), never on the inserter's own tile. Before submitting, check that no two placed entities share a tile.

When an expect check counts machines in a long column or row, center it on the build's midpoint and set the radius to at least half the build's full length plus the machine size, or the end machines fall outside and the count comes up short. If a check reports N-1 of N and the missing one isn't named, suspect the radius before the build.

For a long pole chain to a grid, first locate the grid's actual pole (area/find near its generator) and place the chain's first pole within ~5 tiles of it as a separate explicit place step, not buried inside a big ghosts batch where it may silently fail. Keep chain spacing well under max reach (e.g. 7 for medium poles) so off-by-a-tile positions still link.

When an order implies a production count, end the build with a wait sized to reach it (e.g. 2-3 science assemblers at ~0.1-0.15 packs/s each need 90+ s for 30 packs), not a short 40 s. Make sure every assembler has its own automated feed for every ingredient (no machine left running only on its initial stock). Before planning to reuse or move an entity, confirm its exact position with find (area inserter counts include ones you've already accounted for), never assume a "spare" exists at a guessed tile. When a missing part can't be crafted, take it from a less critical slot in the same broken machine set (e.g. move an output inserter to the input side) instead of guessing.
